reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 oxide layer via thermal shock and its link to improved tribocorrosion resistance in an AlCrTiZrMo HEA film, but the hypothesis generalizes this to a broader class of HEAs and to a 'controlled thermal shock annealing' intervention without evidence that the mechanism is transferable or that the oxide acts as a low-friction interface.
premises: Thermal shock annealing of AlCrTiZrMo HEA film forms a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer
This oxide layer provides oxidation resistance at 800°C in air
The annealed film shows best tribocorrosion resistance in friction-corrosion coupling
The dense oxide layer reduces wear and corrosion simultaneously
